name: Tonga
summary: A Polynesian kingdom united by George Tupou I in 1845; never colonised, though a British protectorate (1900–70).

knownFor.label: Never colonised
knownFor.note: The only Pacific kingdom never colonised.

knownFor.label: Ta’ovala
knownFor.note: Woven mat worn round the waist.

location.value: About 171 islands in the South Pacific, south of Samoa and east of Fiji; about 750 km² of land.

terrain.value: Volcanic islands with high peaks and low coral islands with reefs and lagoons.

climate.value: Tropical, hot and humid, with a cyclone season from November to April.

resources.value: Fish, coconuts, squash and vanilla for export, root crops such as yams, and tourism.

disasters.value: The Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha’apai eruption and tsunami of January 2022; cyclones such as Gita (2018).

population.value: About 100,000–105,000 people in the early 2020s, with many more Tongans living abroad.

urbanisation.value: Most people live in villages; Nuku’alofa on Tongatapu is the capital and only large town.

disease.value: High rates of obesity, diabetes and heart disease, among the highest in the world.

migration.value: Many live in New Zealand, Australia and the US.

economicBase.value: Remittances from Tongans abroad, farming, fishing and tourism.

tradeRoutes.value: Shipping and flights to New Zealand, Australia and Fiji; squash exports to Japan.

wealth.value: An upper-middle-income country by World Bank measure, though dependent on remittances and aid.

moneyAndTax.value: The pa’anga, introduced in 1967 in place of the pound; taxes include a consumption tax.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A constitutional monarchy; since 2010 most members of parliament are elected by the people.

keyRulers.value: George Tupou I. Queen Sālote Tupou III. Tupou VI.

succession.value: Hereditary in the Tupou dynasty, founded by George Tupou I, usually passing to the eldest son.

stability.value: Riots in Nuku’alofa in 2006 destroyed much of the town centre amid demands for democracy.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: Small armed forces that have served in peacekeeping missions and coalitions abroad.

majorWars.value: Civil wars before unification in 1845; Tongan soldiers served with Allied forces in the Second World War.

territoryChange.value: Little change since 1845; Tonga claimed the Minerva Reefs in 1972.

alliancesRivals.value: Member of the Pacific Islands Forum and the Commonwealth; close ties with New Zealand and Australia.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: High literacy; schools such as Tupou College (founded 1866) and a campus of the University of the South Pacific.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Ferries between island groups, flights from Fua’amotu airport, and an undersea internet cable.

religion.value: Mostly Christian; the Free Wesleyan Church is the largest, with Latter-day Saints and Catholics.

languageWriting.value: Tongan and English are the official languages; Tongan is written in the Latin alphabet.

artsArchitecture.value: Tapa (ngatu) bark cloth, fine woven mats, and the lakalaka dance.

socialStructure.value: The king, hereditary nobles and commoners; the 1875 constitution gave commoner men rights to land.

sharedIdentity.value: A strong national identity around the monarchy, the church and Tongan language and customs.

dailyLife.value: Families live in village houses; feasts cooked in an ’umu earth oven, and Sunday is a day of rest by law.

neighbours.value: Fiji, Samoa, Niue, New Zealand and Australia.

ideasReligions.value: Methodism, spread by Wesleyan missionaries in the 1800s, became the main faith after George Tupou I converted.

colonisation.value: British protectorate (1900–70) but never a colony.

peakPeriod.value: The reign of Queen Sālote Tupou III (1918–65), a time of stability and national pride.

declineSignals.value: None; challenges include emigration, natural disasters and debates over democracy.

outcome.value: Still in existence as an independent kingdom, fully self-governing since the protectorate ended in 1970.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
